questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have family in Normandie and my mother is french. I have always frequented Paris, and wanted to know more about my social heritage.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was not the easiest, there is a lot of papers to fill out and some contradictions in the sequence of papers to be filled out that seems different from Copenhagen to Sorbonne. Luckily people were quick at answering questions. 
The whole Erasmus part was easy, and the Mobility-system is good.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is a Erasmus office at Sorbonne, with two very nice coworkers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is a Cité Universitaire with houses from every nationality. I searched directly to the Danish house, but there are lots of houses and possibilities.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a big kitchen, very well equiped. Grocery shopping just around the corner.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend it, as it is a very social place, lots of acitivites, sports and parties. Easy way to find new friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at Sorbonne is a bit oldschool and a bit confusing I would say. They have a portal for registration with many documents to upload, documents that are not necesarely available to us. You have to be good at reaching out to find answers.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an office that takes care of exchange students to Sorbonne, which functions well (or they answer you pretty quickly).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got my first priority.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't panic with the confusing system, it will work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level very high, and we had a lot of extra lessons at the hospital. I felt that it was very important to them to include the students in the working rutines and they wanted to teach us things.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found it more "hardcore", and more demanding, which was a bit tough as an exchange student. But I also think that I learned a lot more from this style of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Neuroanesthesia and reanimation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the one course I took.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not any special.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is not cheap to go out in Paris, but it is worth to prioritize in your budget.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At the campus area there were lots of sports activitites, tennis courts, parties, a theater, a swimming area. Also the houses did expositions.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sports subscription!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Walk around in Marais, Montmarte, Canal Saint-Martin. Visit museums and go for vintageshopping.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, since I have french roots. I think that it could be more difficult if you are not used to the culture, and there is not at lot of mercy for the students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't socialize with local students because I had so much social life in my house. But I would say that they are very interested in you, and if you want to interact with them, they would love to!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I would say that it was rather easy, but getting used to the "no-mercy"-part is probably the hardest. Not taking it personal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The easy lifestyle, going out on a weekday for some food and wine. Things seem easy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Practice french before going, live at the cité universitaire and prioritize food/wine/going-out in your budget (search a lot of scholarships before going!)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid of the teaching style, it is the way they work in France and it is not that you are a bad student.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get to know a lot of great people and enjoy Paris.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The more hardcore approach to the students, which the french students are used to, but can be hard on exchange students as they 1) are not as comfortable in the language, and 2) are not used to this style of learning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
